title: Grateful Dead Live at Saenger Performing Arts Center on 1982-09-09
source: Recording Info: Beyer M160 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-C90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Sony TC-K677ES) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/48k) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2.1 -> FLAC/16; Recorded by Frank Streeter; All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller

ai_review.summary: Lively audience tape from the Saenger ’82 with rambunctious Samson & Delilah and Feel Like a Stranger; sound good but the Uncle John’s‑to‑Samson segue divides listeners.
ai_review.review: The recording captures an energetic 1982 show at the Saenger Theatre, highlighted by wild renditions of “Samson & Delilah” and “Feel Like a Stranger.”  Reviewers praise the clear, lively audience mix—especially the first five songs—but note that the unusual sandwich of Uncle John’s Band into Samson isn’t to everyone’s taste.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong show energy and standout performances with good audience sound quality, offset by a few negative comments about set‑list sequencing.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear and lively audience tape; first five songs described as sounding 'dam good.' No major flaws noted, though some prefer it over any soundboard mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The only contentious point is the rare Uncle John’s → Samson sandwich, which some fans find odd.
